get.description:
The public half of the signing key.

Served to anybody: that is what a public key is for, and it is how the AI
platform validates a token without this service and that one sharing a
secret.

schema.title: Response Jwks Endpoint  Well Known Jwks Json Get

get.description:
Where to find the issuer and its keys.

Deliberately not a full OpenID Provider — there is no authorisation-code
flow here. It publishes what a relying party needs to validate a token it
has been handed, and advertises no endpoints that do not exist.

schema.title: Response Openid Configuration  Well Known Openid Configuration Get

get.summary: Branding for the login page and the application form
get.description:
Unauthenticated, and holds nothing but branding.

The login page needs a name and a logo before anybody has signed in. What
it must not be able to read is anything about the school's money or its
children, which is why this is served by a SECURITY DEFINER function with
a fixed column list rather than by a query against `school`.

post.summary: Send a one-time code by SMS
post.description:
How everybody without a password gets in.

The response is identical whether or not the number belongs to anybody at
the school. A 404 here would turn this route into a way to ask which
parents a school has.

post.summary: Sign in with a one-time code

post.description:
Exchange the refresh cookie for a new pair.

The old token is spent in the process. A token presented twice means two
parties hold it, and the service cuts every session for that user — so a
401 here can mean "your cookie is stale" or "somebody copied it", and the
client's answer to both is the same: sign in again.

Always 204. Signing out of a session that has already expired is not a
problem worth showing somebody who is leaving.

get.description:
The shell's first call after sign-in.

The name comes from the database rather than the token: a token lives
fifteen minutes, and somebody who corrects the spelling of their own name
should not have to wait that long to see it.

post.description:
Ends every session, including this one, on purpose: somebody changing
their password after a scare must not leave a thief's session alive.

post.summary: Cross to aibeyondschools.co.tz already signed in
post.description:
The route the whole project is for.

A student taps a homework link, this mints a two-minute token for the AI
platform, and they arrive already signed in. A second login screen at that
moment would lose most of a cohort.

The redirect URL is built here rather than accepted from the caller: a
signed token plus a client-chosen destination is an open redirect that
leaks the token to whoever asked for it.

get.summary: The authorisation model, as the server sees it
get.description:
What each role may do.

Served so the staff app can build its navigation from the server's answer
instead of keeping a second copy of the permission matrix that drifts from
this one. Readable by any signed-in user: it describes the model, not
anybody's data.

schema.title: Response Roles Api V1 Auth Roles Get

post.summary: Set a password with a code instead of the old one
post.description:
The other half of `/otp/start` with `purpose=password_reset`.

`/password` cannot serve either screen that needs this: somebody who has
forgotten a password cannot supply the current one, and somebody setting
their first never had one. The code is the proof, and it can only have
gone to the number already on the record.

Answers the same way for a number nobody has and a code that was wrong.
Whether a number belongs to a family at this school is not something an
unauthenticated page may be used to find out.

patch.description:
A partial update: only the fields present in the body are touched.

`exclude_unset` matters here. Without it, a form that posts five fields
would clear every other setting to its default, including the two arrears
switches — which is how a school ends up withholding report cards nobody
asked it to withhold.

schema.title: Response List Years Api V1 Academic Years Get

post.summary: Move the school into this year
post.description:
Invoicing and promotion both pivot on this flag, so the change is
audited with the year's label in the note.

schema.title: Response List Terms Api V1 Academic Years  Year Id  Terms Get

put.description:
The whole set at once, because no-overlap and in-date-order are
properties of the set rather than of any one term.

schema.title: Response Replace Terms Api V1 Academic Years  Year Id  Terms Put

get.summary: The level ladder, the exit cohorts, and what is wrong with them
get.description:
What the promotion engine will ask, available to a screen first.

The problems come back with the data on purpose. In 2027 a primary school
holds two exit cohorts at once, and the difference between "correctly
configured for the transition" and "somebody forgot a cohort" is exactly
what a head of academics needs to see in September rather than December.

schema.title: Response List Levels Api V1 Academic Levels Get

post.description:
Answers with the whole ladder, not just the new rung.

A level is only meaningful in relation to the others — what sits above it,
whether its order collides — so the response is the thing the screen has to
redraw anyway, with any new problems attached.

put.summary: Record which cohorts leave at the end of a year
put.description:
The most consequential setting in this module.

A list rather than a single value, because 2027 has two: Standard 7
finishing the old seven-year cycle and Standard 6 finishing the new
six-year one, both sitting the PSLE in the same year.

schema.title: Response List Streams Api V1 Academic Streams Get

post.summary: Add a stream to a level

get.summary: Classes, with how many children are in each
get.description:
Defaults to the current year: that is what a school means by "the
classes", and asking every caller to pass a year invites the bug where one
screen shows last year's.

schema.title: Response List Class Groups Api V1 Academic Class Groups Get

put.summary: Put a teacher in front of a class
put.description:
An authorisation change as much as an administrative one: a class
teacher may read every child in their class.

schema.title: Response List Subjects Api V1 Academic Subjects Get
Response List Teaching Assignments Api V1 Academic Teaching Assignments Get

post.summary: Give a teacher a subject in a class
post.description:
One teacher per subject per class, enforced by a unique index: two
people able to enter the same mark means nobody can say whose it was.

delete.summary: Take a subject off a teacher

get.description:
Search by name or admission number, filter by class, boarding or bus.

A teacher's view is narrowed to their own classes by the service, not by
the client: a list endpoint that returns the school and trusts the caller
to filter is a list endpoint that leaks.

post.description:
The path for a pupil who arrived with a transfer letter. The ordinary
path is the admissions funnel.

get.description:
Everything the profile screen draws, in one answer.

Health is present only for a caller holding `health:read`, and null rather
than absent so the client can tell "not allowed to see" from "nothing
recorded".

One row per academic year. Promotion writes a new row rather than
changing the old one, which is why a report card from two years ago can
still say which class it was earned in.

schema.title: Response Enrolment History Api V1 Students  Student Id  Enrolments Get

post.summary: Close a child's place at the school
post.description:
The enrolment is closed, never deleted, and the student record stays:
a school asked for a transfer letter two years later has to answer, and
arrears do not vanish because a child left.

get.summary: Who to contact about this child

schema.title: Response Student Guardians Api V1 Students  Student Id  Guardians Get

post.summary: Link a guardian to this child
post.description:
Reuses the person if the phone number is already known, which is what
makes a parent with three children one guardian and three links.

delete.description:
Refused for the last guardian on a child: nobody to contact is the one
state this must not be able to produce.

get.description:
Behind `health:read`, and the read itself is audited.

Children's health data is sensitive personal data under the Personal Data
Protection Act, 2022, so "who opened this child's health record" is a
question a school may have to answer.

schema.title: Response Student Health Api V1 Students  Student Id  Health Get
Response Emergency Contacts Api V1 Students  Student Id  Emergency Contacts Get

put.description:
The whole list at once, because the ordering is the point: three
numbers in no particular order is three numbers nobody knows which to ring
first.

schema.title: Response Set Emergency Contacts Api V1 Students  Student Id  Emergency Contacts Put
Response Student Documents Api V1 Students  Student Id  Documents Get

post.description:
Step two of two.

Storage is asked what actually arrived rather than trusting what the
client said it would send, which is what makes the size limit real and
what stops a record existing for an upload that never finished.

post.summary: Get a URL to upload a document to
post.description:
Step one of two. The client PUTs the file straight to storage.

The bytes never come through this API: a four-megabyte photograph through
an application container ties up a worker for the length of a 3G upload,
and a school's intake day is several hundred of them.

get.summary: A short-lived link to one document
get.description:
Generated per request, never stored.

The bucket is private so that opening a child's birth certificate is an
act with a permission attached rather than a URL anybody holding it can
follow forever.

get.summary: What is still missing from this record
get.description:
Built from three sources — the core fields, the school's own document
checklist, and whichever custom fields it marked as required — by the same
function the admissions queue uses.

put.summary: Set this school's own fields for a child
put.description:
Each value is checked against its field's declared kind before it is
stored. A number field that accepted "about 40" would be a column nobody
can add up.

schema.title: Response Set Student Fields Api V1 Students  Student Id  Fields Put

post.summary: Put a child in a class for a year
post.description:
Refused if the child already has an open enrolment.

The database allows one active enrolment per child, so rather than quietly
rewriting last year's row this says so and leaves the decision — close it,
or let a promotion run move them — with the person making it.

patch.summary: Change this year's class, boarding or bus
patch.description:
All of these are per-year facts.

A child who moves from Blue to Green in March, starts boarding in May and
comes off the bus in September has one row that tells the truth about this
year — and last year's row is untouched, which is what a closed year
means.

get.description:
The parent portal's landing screen: every child, with what each owes.

One query rather than one per child. This is the page a guardian opens in
a queue at the bursar's office on a weak connection, and four numbers per
child is the whole point of it.

schema.title: Response My Children Api V1 Guardians Me Children Get

get.description:
Searched by name or phone, which is what a bursar has in front of them
when a payment arrives with no reference.

get.summary: What this school is asking for
get.description:
Served unauthenticated, from the subdomain, and holds nothing about any
child: the levels on offer, the papers to bring, and the school's own
questions.

Only levels with a published fee structure appear — a level nobody can be
quoted a deposit for is a level nobody should be able to apply to.

post.summary: Send a code to this number
post.description:
Step one. The number is verified before anything else is collected.

The answer is the same whether or not an application already exists for
that number: a different response would turn this into a way to ask which
families have applied.

post.summary: Verify the code and start or resume the form
post.description:
Step two, and the only place a session is handed out.

Resumes an open application for that number rather than starting a new
one — a parent who lost the page at question nine comes back to question
nine.

patch.description:
Called as the parent types. Nothing here is required.

Saved against the verified phone number, so the form survives a dropped
connection, a closed browser and a flat battery.

post.description:
Checks the shortest honest list: a name, a date of birth, a sex, a level
and a guardian who can be reached.

Screening for a child the school already has runs on the way in, so the
registrar opens a queue that already says which applications look like
duplicates.

post.summary: Get a URL to upload a document to
post.description:
Step one of two. The parent's phone PUTs the photograph straight to
storage; the bytes never come through this API.

The best moment to get a birth certificate is while somebody is sitting
with the form open and the certificate in their hand. Every week after
that is a phone call.

Step two. Storage is asked what actually arrived rather than trusting
what the client said it would send — a presigned PUT cannot enforce a
length, and on a 3G connection a real fraction of uploads never finish.

Answers with the whole form state, so the checklist on the parent's screen
updates without a second request.

get.description:
Oldest first, because the number a registrar sorts by is how long a
family has been waiting.

Defaults to the two states somebody is expected to act on. A queue that
showed every application ever would be a queue nobody opens.

What the dashboard draws. The step worth watching is offered to
enrolled: a deposit payment is what converts an application into a
pupil.

post.description:
An explicit step, because the next one burns an admission number and
the school should be able to say who decided this child is new.

Issues the admission number and raises the deposit invoice.

The number comes from a locked per-school sequence and is burnt here
rather than at enrolment, because the offer letter carries it — a family
written to with a number keeps it.

A reason is required: a family that rings to ask why deserves an
answer, and the registrar who declined it may not be the one who takes
the call.

post.summary: Record the deposit, which accepts the place
post.description:
The only way an application becomes accepted.

Phase 1 has no aggregator, so a bursar records the money and the
application moves itself. There is no accept button to press by mistake,
and a place nobody has paid for cannot look accepted in the funnel.

post.summary: Turn an accepted application into a pupil
post.description:
One transaction: a child, a guardian, an enrolment and a login.

All of it or none of it. Half of this is a pupil the roll cannot find or a
parent who cannot sign in to pay — and the deposit has already been taken
by this point, so there is no graceful way to leave it half done.

schema.title: Response Structures Api V1 Fees Structures Get

post.description: It begins as a draft, and nothing can be invoiced from a draft.

get.summary: One fee structure and its items
get.description:
The only way to reopen a draft.

The list says a structure has five items; this says which five. Without it
a half-finished draft could be read back only by whoever still had the
create response in front of them, so closing the tab lost the work.

put.description:
Refused once published: invoices already raised would otherwise change
retrospectively, and a parent who photographed a bill must find the same
figure on it three weeks later.

post.description:
An empty structure cannot be published: a term run would bill every
child nothing and look as though it worked.
Refused once published. A draft, though, has billed nobody.

Previews by default.

`dry_run` is true unless asked otherwise: a run over 500 children is not
something to start by accident, and the preview is how a bursar finds out
that Standard 6's structure is still a draft before the invoices go out.

Repeatable. A child who already has an invoice for the term is skipped, so
running it again after an interruption is the safe recovery rather than
the thing that double-bills a school.

get.description:
Status and ageing are computed against `as_of`, which defaults to today.

Passed in rather than assumed so a statement produced for last month is
read against last month.

get.summary: One invoice, its lines and its payments

get.description: Across years, because arrears follow the child.

post.summary: Void an invoice that should not have been raised
post.description:
Refused once money is against it: a payment attached to a bill that
officially does not exist is worse than the mistake. Write a credit note
instead.

Another line, never an edit. The original charge stays, so the bill a
parent photographed and the bill the school holds remain one document.

get.description:
One row per child, worst first.

A bursar chasing arrears rings a family rather than a document, so three
overdue bills for one child is one phone call and one row.

The dashboard's money tiles, read against `as_of` — today by default,
and the same day the arrears list beneath them is read against.

post.description:
A named, audited entry — the whole payment system in Phase 1.

An overpayment is not refused: the remainder is the family's credit and
stays visible on the payment rather than being quietly absorbed.

get.description:
The dashboard's first "needs your attention" row.

A payment with no reference from a number the school does not hold is
recorded, visible, and waiting for a bursar. Dropping it on the floor or
guessing an invoice for it is how a month-end stops balancing.

schema.title: Response Suspense Api V1 Payments Suspense Get

get.description:
The dashboard's second card, newest first.

Reversed payments are left out: a reversal is not a receipt, and a feed
that showed one would have a bursar chasing money that was already undone.

schema.title: Response Recent Api V1 Payments Recent Get

post.summary: Attach a payment to the invoice it belongs to
post.description:
A bursar's decision, not the system's guess.

Nothing picks between two siblings with open balances: the wrong choice
takes an afternoon to unpick and a parent's phone call to discover. Who
decided is recorded.

ApplicationDetailResponse.title: ApplicationDetailResponse
ApplicationDetailResponse.description: The registrar's view: the parent's view plus what screening found.

ApplyDocument.title: ApplyDocument
ApplyDocument.description:
One file a parent has attached.

`file_url` is the storage key and is deliberately absent: it is not a URL
anybody can open, and sending it would put an object key in a page a
stranger reaches.

ApplyFieldOption.title: ApplyFieldOption
ApplyFieldOption.description: One of a school's own questions, for the form to render.

ApplyOptionsResponse.title: ApplyOptionsResponse
ApplyOptionsResponse.description:
Everything the public form needs to draw itself.

Served unauthenticated, from the subdomain, and holds nothing about any
child: the levels on offer, the papers to bring, and the school's own
questions.

ApplySaveRequest.title: ApplySaveRequest
ApplySaveRequest.description:
Save progress. Every field is optional, on purpose.

A half-finished application is a legal row rather than a validation error,
which is what lets a parent stop at question nine on a weak connection and
come back by code.

ApplyStartRequest.title: ApplyStartRequest
ApplyStartRequest.description:
The phone number a code goes to.

Verified before anything else is collected, which kills most junk
applications and is the only credential this parent will have.

ApplyStateResponse.title: ApplyStateResponse
ApplyStateResponse.description: What the form shows a parent: where they are, and what is left.

ArrearsRow.title: ArrearsRow
ArrearsRow.description:
One child, not one invoice: a bursar chasing arrears rings a family,
and three overdue bills for one child is one phone call.

ChecklistResponse.title: ChecklistResponse
ChecklistResponse.description:
What is still missing from a child's record.

`complete` is computed by the same function the admissions queue uses, so
the two screens cannot disagree about what complete means.

CreditNoteRequest.title: CreditNoteRequest
CreditNoteRequest.description: Take something off a bill without rewriting it.

DocumentCreateRequest.title: DocumentCreateRequest
DocumentCreateRequest.description:
Record a file that has already been uploaded.

The bytes never pass through this API: the client PUTs them to storage
with the presigned URL, then confirms here. The service asks storage what
actually arrived rather than trusting the size and type declared earlier —
a presigned PUT cannot enforce a length.

DownloadUrlResponse.title: DownloadUrlResponse
DownloadUrlResponse.description:
A short-lived link to one document.

Generated per request rather than stored. The bucket is private precisely
so that reading a child's birth certificate is an act with a permission
attached.

EnrolRequest.title: EnrolRequest
EnrolRequest.description: The last step: which class, and whether they board.

EnrolmentHistoryRow.title: EnrolmentHistoryRow
EnrolmentHistoryRow.description: One year of a child's history, as the profile timeline draws it.

EnrolmentOutcome.title: EnrolmentOutcome
EnrolmentOutcome.description:
What happened to one child in one year.

ACTIVE is the only one that means "still here". The database enforces at
most one active enrolment per student with a partial unique index, which is
cheaper than any amount of application-level care.

EnrolmentUpdateRequest.title: EnrolmentUpdateRequest
EnrolmentUpdateRequest.description: This year's facts. All of them are per-year by design.

ExitLevelsReplaceRequest.title: ExitLevelsReplaceRequest
ExitLevelsReplaceRequest.description:
Which cohorts leave at the end of a year.

A list, because 2027 has two: Standard 7 finishing the old seven-year cycle
and Standard 6 finishing the new six-year one, sitting the same examination
in the same year.

FeeFrequency.title: FeeFrequency
FeeFrequency.description:
How often an item is billed.

PER_TERM is billed on every term invoice, ANNUAL once a year on the first
term's invoice, and ONE_OFF only when a child joins — which is what makes
the admission fee and the uniform charge land on the deposit invoice and
never again.

FeeItemModel.title: FeeItemModel
FeeItemModel.description: One line of a structure: what it is, how much, and how often.

FeeStructureRow.title: FeeStructureRow
FeeStructureRow.description:
A structure as the settings screen lists it.

The item count and total come along because a structure with no items is
the commonest reason a term run finds nothing to bill.

FieldKind.title: FieldKind
FieldKind.description:
What a custom field holds.

Deliberately five. Each one has an obvious input on a phone and an obvious
validation; a sixth ("anything") would mean nothing could be checked.

FieldValuesRequest.title: FieldValuesRequest
FieldValuesRequest.description:
A school's own fields, keyed by the field's key.

Each value is checked against its field's declared kind before it is
stored — a number field that accepted "about 40" would be a column nobody
can add up.

FunnelResponse.title: FunnelResponse
FunnelResponse.description:
What the dashboard draws.

A deposit payment is what converts an application into an enrolment, which
is why the step between offered and enrolled is the one worth watching.

GuardianChildResponse.title: GuardianChildResponse
GuardianChildResponse.description: One child, as their guardian's own screen shows them.

GuardianDetails.title: GuardianDetails
GuardianDetails.description:
The person. Matched on phone, which is what makes a parent with three
children one guardian and three links.

GuardianLinkDetails.title: GuardianLinkDetails
GuardianLinkDetails.description:
The four decisions that hang off the link, not off the person.

A father can be the primary contact for one child and not for another, and
whichever guardian receives the invoices is a per-child choice.

GuardianOnStudent.title: GuardianOnStudent
GuardianOnStudent.description: A guardian as the student profile shows them.

HandoffRequest.title: HandoffRequest
HandoffRequest.description:
Which child is crossing over.

Required for a guardian, who may have several, and ignored for a student,
who can only ever be themselves.

HandoffResponse.title: HandoffResponse
HandoffResponse.description: The token that carries a student across to aibeyondschools.co.tz.

HealthResponse.title: HealthResponse
HealthResponse.description: Medical detail. Only ever served to a caller holding `health:read`.

InvoiceDetailResponse.title: InvoiceDetailResponse
InvoiceDetailResponse.description:
One bill, its lines and the money against it.

Assembled server-side because the three have to agree: a parent looking at
a total that does not match the lines above it stops trusting every other
number on the page.

InvoiceLineKind.title: InvoiceLineKind
InvoiceLineKind.description:
A line is a charge, a discount or a credit note, and the sign follows
from the kind rather than from whoever typed the amount.

InvoiceRow.title: InvoiceRow
InvoiceRow.description: One line of the fees screen.

LadderResponse.title: LadderResponse
LadderResponse.description:
The ladder and everything wrong with it, in one answer.

The problems travel with the data rather than behind a second call, because
the academic settings screen shows both and a school that only sees the
happy version finds out in December.

LevelStage.title: LevelStage
LevelStage.description: The four stages of the 1+6+4+2/3 structure the country is moving to.

ManualPaymentRequest.title: ManualPaymentRequest
ManualPaymentRequest.description:
Money a bursar has in hand.

Phase 1 has no aggregator, so this is how a deposit becomes a pupil. The
receipt number is required and unique per school: entering the same
receipt twice is caught rather than doubling a credit.

OtpSentResponse.title: OtpSentResponse
OtpSentResponse.description:
What a code request answers.

Never says whether the number is known to the school: the response is the
same for a guardian's phone and a stranger's, because the difference is
exactly what an attacker would be probing for.

PasswordResetRequest.title: PasswordResetRequest
PasswordResetRequest.description:
Set a password by proving the phone, not by knowing the old one.

Serves both screens that need it: somebody who has forgotten a password
cannot supply the current one, and somebody setting their first never had
one. The code can only have gone to the number already on the record.

Permission.title: Permission
Permission.description:
Named capabilities, not CRUD on tables.

PAYMENT_RECORD_MANUAL rather than payment:create, because the interesting
question is never "may this person write to a table" but "may this person
move money", and the two drift apart the moment a second way to move money
exists.

PrincipalResponse.title: PrincipalResponse
PrincipalResponse.description:
Who the caller is, as the staff app's shell needs them.

Permissions are sent as a list rather than left for the client to derive
from the role. The server owns the authorisation model; a client that
recomputes it is a client that will eventually disagree with it, and the
screens only use it to decide what to show.

QueueRowResponse.title: QueueRowResponse
QueueRowResponse.description: One line of the review queue.

RecentPayment.title: RecentPayment
RecentPayment.description:
One line of the dashboard's "Payments received" card.

Carries the child and the class rather than the invoice reference: a bursar
recognises "Neema Mwanjala, Standard 4 Blue" and recognises nothing at all
about INV/Term1/0184.

RecordPaymentRequest.title: RecordPaymentRequest
RecordPaymentRequest.description:
Money a bursar has in hand.

Phase 1 has no aggregator, so this is how fees get settled. The receipt is
required and unique per school: entering the same one twice is caught
rather than doubling a credit.

RollRowResponse.title: RollRowResponse
RollRowResponse.description:
One line of the students screen.

Carries the class and the fee totals because the roll shows both, and
because a list that made the client fetch them per row would be a list
nobody waits for on a 3G connection.

SchoolBrandResponse.title: SchoolBrandResponse
SchoolBrandResponse.description:
What the login page and the public application form may know.

This is served unauthenticated, so it holds branding and nothing else — no
fee settings, no counts, nothing about a single child.

SchoolUpdateRequest.title: SchoolUpdateRequest
SchoolUpdateRequest.description:
Everything a school admin may change about their own school.

Absent from this list, on purpose: `subdomain`, because it is the tenant
key and changing it would break every bookmark and every parent's saved
link; `status`, because suspending a school is a platform decision; and
`currency`, because invoices already exist in it.

StatementResponse.title: StatementResponse
StatementResponse.description:
Every bill a child has ever had, across years.

Across years because arrears follow the child: a statement that began at
the current year would not explain the balance on it.

StudentCreateRequest.title: StudentCreateRequest
StudentCreateRequest.description:
Admit a child by hand.

No admission number: it is issued from a locked per-school sequence, not
accepted from a form, so two registrars admitting at once cannot mint the
same one.

StudentProfileResponse.title: StudentProfileResponse
StudentProfileResponse.description: Everything the profile screen draws, in one answer.

SuspensePayment.title: SuspensePayment
SuspensePayment.description: Money that arrived with nothing to match it.

TermRunRequest.title: TermRunRequest
TermRunRequest.description:
Raise a term's invoices.

`dry_run` defaults to true on purpose. A run over 500 children is not
something to start by accident, and a bursar should see what it would do —
including which levels have no published structure — before any invoice
exists.

TermsReplaceRequest.title: TermsReplaceRequest
TermsReplaceRequest.description:
A year's terms, all of them.

The rules worth enforcing — no overlaps, numbered in date order, inside the
year — are properties of the whole set, so the whole set arrives together.
Sending them one at a time would let a school get halfway into a calendar
that cannot be reconciled.

TokenResponse.title: TokenResponse
TokenResponse.description:
The access token and who it belongs to.

The refresh token is absent on purpose: it is set as an httpOnly cookie
and never passes through JavaScript, so a cross-site script cannot read a
fortnight of access out of the page.

UploadTicketRequest.title: UploadTicketRequest
UploadTicketRequest.description:
What the client is about to upload.

Declared up front so an impossible upload is refused before a parent on a
weak connection has sent four megabytes.

UploadTicketResponse.title: UploadTicketResponse
UploadTicketResponse.description:
Where to PUT the file, and what to send with it.

`object_key` is chosen by the server and echoed back to be confirmed. A
client that could choose its own key is a client that could overwrite
another school's object.
